comments.content: @sergfeldman how is this coming along? I haven't heard updates in awhile but this was "assigned" over a month ago.
I understand that credit cards are less common to issue. Let's just do a debit card. What's the status for issuing debit cards?

I understood that we were eligible for Visa's partner program - remember when I gave you my login credentials? I would be interested to invest/work with Stripe or Visa directly over the other options I can think of. 
I also think that beyond just the physical cards, we should offer digital cards that can be used for online/digital phone (NFC/Apple Pay) payments. 
Lastly I would like to see a feature, like how privacy.com does it, where the users have the ability to generate unique card numbers for privacy and money management purposes.
We can have users deposit their Ubiquity Dollars into our (centralized) platform where we can debit their dollars (off chain) to settle card payments. This gives our dollar another utility, for real world spending, independent of the DevPool conveniences we have explicitly discussed in the past.
---

But for now this is what I think makes sense in terms of vision. I hope that clarifies my perspective.

comments.content:
Airwallex 
Your use case is definitely fine, there's just some scrutiny when it comes to onboarding web3 adjacent companies. Considering you're going to use the platform just for cards though, it should be ok. 
Airwallex positive and negative reviews 
https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/discussions/307#discussioncomment-5909124
API documentation
https://www.airwallex.com/docs/api#/Introduction
Aspire

I wrote inquiries to 6 new card issuers.
So far, no new response has been received.
Next, I will contact banks directly located in the British Virgin Islands.

After analyzing our case, Airwallex decided to refuse cooperation specifically in card issuing.
The official reason is the registration in the British Virgin Islands.
Some facts to better understand their logic:
- They waited for the KYC Onboarding Team to look into our case.
- They mention some scrutiny when it comes to onboarding Web3-related companies.
- They stated that requirements for opening a business account without issuing cards are lower.

I contacted via emails all the known banks in British Virgin Islands 
https://thebanks.eu/banks-by-country/British-Virgin-Islands#operating_banks
https://nationalbank.vg/
https://www.cibcfcib.com/
https://vg.vpbank.com/
https://www.popular.vi/contact-us/
https://republicbankbvi.com/
https://www.1firstbank.com/vi/
https://www.bankasia.com/

After conversation with Unlimint:
They are ready to proceed with our case, but only able to provide Banking as a Service to businesses and individuals registered within the EEA.

Sure, we can! 
After the MiCA legislation in 2024, the European Union will be one of the well-regulated crypto jurisdictions that simplifies the cooperation on card issuing. 
At the same time, the operational activity of this business entity will be partially limited by the European Economic Area.
Of course, we will be able to serve companies from any country except sanctioned. 
For corporate card issuing, the employees in the majority of cases should have established business relationships with this business entity (employee, contractor, etc)
For the consumer (not corporate) cards, a business entity registered in the European Economic Area can issue cards for the European Economic Area.
You can see this on the Gnosis Cards example - they will launch in the European Economic Area first, then gradually expand in other countries 
https://gnosispay.com/#how-it-works
![Gnosis cards](https://github.com/ubiquity/card-issuance/assets/15567379/e71fe3cf-8b47-4f16-979b-93b01fd9e616)
Each jurisdiction requires its BIN sponsors, KYC process, etc, which is why the "traditional" way of global card issuance is hard.
